Cifrado y autenticación se combinan, y e: Encryption and authentication are combined, and the order matters. What has held up in practice is encrypt and then seal: the tag is computed over the ciphertext, Bob checks it before decrypting anything, and if it does not match, he does not touch the message. Los modos de <strong>cifrado autenticado: Authenticated encryption modes do everything in one operation and also allow the sealing of associated data that travels in the clear, such as a header with the recipient: it is not encrypted, but if it changes, the tag fails. AES-GCM, which is CTR plus a MAC computed with products in $\text{GF}(2^{128})$, today protects most secure connections; ChaCha20-Poly1305 does the same on phones without AES instructions.
Mark Wegman y Larry Carter definieron en: Mark Wegman and Larry Carter defined authentication codes with provable security in 1981, with an idea that reappears in Poly1305. Mihir Bellare, Ran Canetti and Hugo Krawczyk published HMAC in 1996, with a proof that its security rests on weak properties of the hash, and it was standardised the following year. Authenticated encryption modes arrived from 2000 on; GCM, by David McGrew and John Viega, is from 2004, and Poly1305, by Daniel Bernstein, from 2005.

Un <strong>código de autenticación de me: A message authentication code, MAC, is a short number, the tag, computed from the message and a shared key. Alice sends message and tag; Bob recomputes the tag with his copy of the key and compares. If it matches, the message is from somebody with the key and has not been touched. The property demanded is that, without the key, nobody can produce a valid tag for any new message, even having seen thousands of message-tag pairs.
